anomalies.observed: R85 is valued "24k", but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part ("24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor", MPN FRC0805J240TSD, where "240" is the 24Ω code). The value field and the part identity disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: A resistor whose value field matches its part number and description. If 24k is intended, the MPN and description should be 24kΩ; if 24Ω is intended, the value should be 24R.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R85") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: The resistor between VOUTP and VOUTN will be built either as 24k or as 24Ω. A 24Ω part would load the supply heavily and could overheat or drain it; a 24k part is a different bleed or balance network than the parts list describes.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three green status LEDs D3, D6 and D7 all sit on net /NET0053, and that net contains only these three anode pins. Nothing supplies it, so the LED anodes have no supply connection. Their cathodes are driven through R71, R96 and R68 from CM4 status outputs (nLED3, PI_nLED_Activity, nLED2).
anomalies.expected: The common anode net of these status LEDs should be tied to +3V3 (or another supply) through a resistor or directly, as is done for the other indicator LEDs (for example D1 via R75 from +3V3, D15 from +3V3).
anomalies.impact: D3, D6 and D7 cannot light, so the Ethernet link/activity status indication is lost. The isolated anode net is also a sign of a wiring error.

anomalies.observed: The P-channel pass FET Q11 has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on the VBUS input net. Its body diode therefore conducts from +5V toward VBUS when the FET is off. This is the reverse of the other P-channel load switches on the board (Q9, Q10), where the source sits on the +5V input and the drain feeds the load. The LTC4412 SENSE pin (U3.6) is also on the +5V output net.
anomalies.expected: For a reverse-current-blocking ideal-diode path from VBUS to +5V, the FET source should be on the input (VBUS) and the drain on the output (+5V), so that its body diode blocks reverse current from +5V back to VBUS when the FET is off.
anomalies.impact: If the source and drain are reversed, the USB-input ideal-diode path does not block reverse current. The +5V rail can back-feed the USB VBUS net when the USB source is absent, which defeats the protection the LTC4412 stage was added for.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows a resistor value (R85, 24k) that contradicts its 24Ω part number and description, and three status LEDs (D3, D6, D7) whose anode net connects to nothing else, so they have no supply. The USB ideal-diode pass FET Q11 also appears to have its source and drain reversed relative to the other power-path switches; this is less certain.
